text: Sunk City: a VR world generated live by a tiny neural renderer
description: Idea space. None of these ideas are mandatory; they can contradict each other. A stylised, comic, solarpunk VR game on a fast-spinning alien planet, aimed at Steam Frame (OpenXR). Frames are generated by a tiny network based on the previous stereo frames, depth and head motion, instead of triangle rendering.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Pendulum swinging between the rising blocks is more fun and more VR-native than zipping, and keeps the player moving through the net's generated city.

A EUR 30k-scale XR development grant pays for remote GPU training and a production sprint, the two things currently limiting quality (CPU-only training, one run at a time). Refuted if the project's form (art/tech experiment) does not match the funds' commercial criteria.

Positioned as the tiny, on-device, 90 Hz stereo counterpart to 5B world models, a demo draws collaborators, GPU access or funding (the two current limits) within weeks. Refuted if a posted demo gets no contact from people with compute, funds or XR distribution.
Exploring cost/beauty bounds keeps the renderer's art direction alive and finds cheaper, prettier nets
